//: CHUNK BUDGETS — recorded, enforced, and a BUILD FAILURE when exceeded.
M27's deliverable: 'chunk budgets recorded and enforced, so a regression is a build failure
rather than a discovery'. The shape is upstream's — aztec-packages/playground/vite.config.ts
declares a list of { pattern, maxSizeKB, description } and its plugin THROWS on a violation —
and so is the discipline: their limits carry a per-bump log naming what grew and why. Ours is
the `bumps` array, which is data rather than a comment so that a check can read it.
THREE DIVERGENCES FROM UPSTREAM'S, and each comes from this milestone's own wording:
* GZIPPED, because the deliverable says 'recorded gzipped budget' and gzip is what a page
downloads. Raw bytes are recorded beside it in dist/chunks.json so a reader can reproduce
a number with `ls`.
* NO CATCH-ALL. Upstream ends with /.*/ at 5300 KB as a safety net; here a file matched by
no budget FAILS THE BUILD. 'the budget did not catch it' and 'nothing had a budget' are
indistinguishable from the outside.
* PER-ENTRY EAGER TOTALS as well as per-file sizes. A per-file budget cannot see the
regression that matters for DD-11 — a lazily-loaded megabyte moving into the eager set —
because every individual file can stay the same size while the SET grows. `entryBudgets`
is the transitive closure of an entry point's STATIC imports, which is exactly what a page
pays before it does anything.
HEADROOM IS DELIBERATELY SMALL. A budget with three times the headroom is a number nobody has
to think about. These sit just above the measurement of 2026-08-27.

budgets.name: entry-browser
budgets.description: the reference entry point's own module — DD-5's browser surface

budgets.name: entry-testing
budgets.description: browser + the vendored transaction builder and the deterministic clocks

budgets.name: entry-worker
budgets.description: M32: the worker entry's own module — the dev node's dispatcher, the comlink transport and the protocol declarations. The runtime it hosts is in the shared chunks it imports, which is why this number is a kilobyte rather than a hundred.

budgets.name: entry-worker-demo
budgets.description: M32: the worker demo page's own script — the client, the five arms and the main-thread control

budgets.name: entry-wallet
budgets.description: M33: the wallet protocol boundary's own module — the provider, the port connection handler, the null wallet and the vendored protocol types. Upstream's WalletSchema and the crypto it needs are in the shared chunks it imports, which is why this number is kilobytes rather than hundreds.

budgets.name: entry-node
budgets.description: the Node entry: the browser surface plus four declared fs conveniences (DD-5). It carries the shared @aztec code itself because the Node pass does not share chunks with the browser pass; only pino's CommonJS logging stack is external.

budgets.name: shared-chunk
budgets.description: code shared between the browser entry points: @aztec/stdlib, foundation, the orchestration, the AVM host

budgets.name: node-shared-chunk
budgets.description: the Node pass's own shared chunks

budgets.name: protocol-contract-artifact
budgets.description: a canonical protocol-contract artifact, behind upstream's own lazy.js dynamic import. DD-11: these are the 'contract artifacts' that must load lazily. A public transaction reaches FeeJuice only; the two registries are never fetched by the demo at all.

budgets.name: barretenberg-proving-wasm
budgets.description: bb.js's base64-inlined proving wasm, behind its own dynamic import. DD-11: a public-only page never fetches this, which verify_public_only_page_never_fetches_barretenberg asserts on the network log. The budget exists so its SIZE is recorded rather than merely its absence from the eager set.

budgets.name: lazy-crypto-chunk
budgets.description: small chunks viem and @noble split out behind dynamic imports; none is on the public-execution path

entryBudgets.name: browser
entryBudgets.description: THE NUMBER DD-11 IS ABOUT: everything the reference entry point downloads before it can do anything. It must not contain the proving wasm or any contract artifact.

entryBudgets.name: testing
entryBudgets.description: the test harness entry's eager set: browser plus the vendored builder

entryBudgets.name: demo
entryBudgets.description: what the demo page costs on first paint, before avm.wasm is fetched

entryBudgets.name: node
entryBudgets.description: the Node entry's eager set. Larger than the browser entry's only because the Node pass does not share chunks with the browser pass, not because it carries anything the browser entry does not.

entryBudgets.name: worker
entryBudgets.description: M32, and it is the DD-5 number for the worker: everything the WORKER thread downloads before it can do anything. It hosts the same runtime the browser entry does plus comlink and the protocol's zod schemas, and it must contain no more of the proving stack or the contract artifacts than the browser entry does — which is nothing.

entryBudgets.name: worker-demo
entryBudgets.description: what the worker demo page costs on first paint. It carries the main-thread CONTROL as well as the client, so it necessarily reaches the runtime too.

entryBudgets.name: wallet
entryBudgets.description: M33, and it is the number that justifies the wallet boundary being an entry point of its own rather than part of the browser reference. It is what a page pays to speak the wallet protocol: upstream's WalletSchema and every zod codec the fifteen methods name, reached through @aztec/aztec.js. DD-11's rule is that a page which attaches no wallet must not pay it, and the browser entry's own eager set is the control that says it does not.
